title: A locally bijective morphism of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:F\to G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on it. Say that $f$ is locally injective when for every $U$ and $s,t\in F(U)$ with $f(s)=f(t)$, some covering of $U$ makes the restrictions of $s$ and $t$ equal. Say that $f$ is locally surjective when every $t\in G(U)$ lifts to $F$ on some covering of $U$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism if and only if it is locally injective and locally surjective.

source.place: Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso, lines 84-93, and its type-valued proof, lines 43-74

proof.text: Local injectivity implies componentwise injectivity: two sections with equal images agree on a covering, hence agree by separatedness of F. For any section of G choose local lifts by local surjectivity. Their images agree on overlaps by naturality, so injectivity makes the lifts compatible. The sheaf property of F glues them; separatedness of G shows that the glued section maps to the original one. Thus every component of f is bijective, and their inverses are natural, giving an inverse of f.

An isomorphism is componentwise bijective; use the identity covering for local injectivity and local surjectivity. Mathlib packages both directions as Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso (specialized to Type).
